sentenceSets.sentence: She learned to delegate effectively, trusting staff to handle tasks she had once insisted on doing herself.

answerChoices.reasoning: Entrusting means placing confidence in someone else, very close to delegating, but entrusting emphasizes the trust, while delegating emphasizes the assignment of responsibility.
Assigning means allotting or giving a task, nearly synonymous with delegating, but assigning can be more directive, while delegating implies empowering another.
Empowering means giving authority or confidence, close to delegating, but empowering emphasizes granting authority, while delegating emphasizes assigning responsibility.
Authorizing means granting permission or power, close to delegating, but authorizing emphasizes formal permission, while delegating emphasizes assignment of duty.
Committing means entrusting or pledging, related to delegating but emphasizing obligation rather than the assignment of responsibility.
Distributing means dividing and giving out, related to delegating but more about division than assigning responsibility with authority.
Transferring means moving from one place or person to another, related to delegating but more general and not necessarily about authority.
Outsourcing means obtaining from external sources, related to delegating but typically involves external parties, while delegating uses internal staff.
Retaining means keeping or holding, opposite to delegating; the sentence shows she learned to give tasks to others, not retain them.
Monopolizing means keeping exclusive control of, opposite to delegating; she moved from doing all tasks herself to delegating them.
Hoarding means accumulating and keeping, opposite to delegating; the sentence shows she moved from keeping all tasks to herself.

sentenceSets.sentence: The small nation delegated its representative to the international trade conference to negotiate on its behalf.

answerChoices.reasoning: Sending means dispatching or transmitting, close to delegating a representative, but sending does not necessarily convey the assignment of authority and responsibility.
Appointing means assigning to a position, very close to delegating a representative, but appointing is more formal and official.
Authorizing means granting permission or power, close to delegating, but authorizing emphasizes the grant of power rather than the assignment itself.
Designating means officially assigning or appointing, very close to delegating, but designating emphasizes formal assignment rather than empowerment.
Commissioning means ordering or hiring to do something, related to delegating but often more transactional than empowering.
Empowering means giving authority, related to delegating but emphasizing the grant of power rather than the selection and assignment.
Instructing means teaching or giving orders, related to delegating but emphasizing direction rather than empowerment.
Mandating means officially requiring or commanding, related to delegating but emphasizing command rather than empowerment.
Withholding means refusing to provide or release, opposite to delegating; the nation sent its representative, not withheld it.
Recalling means summoning back, opposite to delegating; the nation sent its representative, not recalled it.
Abandoning means leaving without support, opposite to delegating; the nation empowered its representative, not abandoned it.

sentenceSets.sentence: The project manager delegated authority to the team leads, holding them accountable for the success of their individual departments.

answerChoices.reasoning: Entrusting means placing confidence in someone, very close to delegating, but entrusting emphasizes the trust, while delegating emphasizes the assignment of authority.
Granting means giving or allowing, very close to delegating authority, but granting can be passive, while delegating emphasizes active assignment.
Empowering means giving authority or power, nearly synonymous with delegating, but empowering emphasizes the grant of power.
Assigning means allotting or giving responsibility, very close to delegating, but assigning is more neutral, while delegating emphasizes empowerment with accountability.
Transferring means moving from one place or person to another, related to delegating but more general and not necessarily emphasizing accountability.
Distributing means dividing and giving out, related to delegating but more about division than assignment with accountability.
Allocating means distributing or apportioning, related to delegating but emphasizing distribution rather than delegation of authority.
Commissioning means ordering or hiring to do something, related to delegating but often more transactional.
Withholding means refusing to provide, opposite to delegating; the manager granted authority, not withheld it.
Retaining means keeping or holding, opposite to delegating; the manager gave authority to team leads, not retained it.
Monopolizing means keeping exclusive control, opposite to delegating; the manager distributed authority to team leads, not monopolized it.
